Light absorption: Plants absorb light energy from the sun using chlorophyll, a pigment found in organelles called chloroplasts.  2. Water splitting: The absorbed light energy is used to power a process called photolysis, which splits water molecules into oxygen gas and hydrogen ions.  3. Carbon fixation: The hydrogen ions are used to convert carbon dioxide into a usable form, while the oxygen gas is released as a byproduct.  4. Reduction: The carbon dioxide is reduced to a molecule containing carbon and a high-energy electron, which is then used to produce glucose and other sugars.

[Inquiry]
user: Why are we taxed on revenue and companies on profit?
assistant: 
Companies, regardless of their size, are taxed on profits rather than revenues. This means that the method by which profits are earned is irrelevant. Profits are calculated as income minus all expenses incurred to generate that income. It's important to note that profits cannot simply be withdrawn from the company. Revenue is not the same as income; in fact, income is often considered synonymous with profit. Income is the amount of money earned after all expenses are accounted for. Just like individuals, corporations are taxed on their revenue after deducting allowable expenses.
user: Do businesses pay income tax on the salaries they pay to their employees?
assistant: No, businesses do not pay income tax on the salaries they provide to their employees.
user: Do all employers withhold money for income tax?
assistant: Many countries require employers to report their employees' salaries and withhold money for income tax purposes. In the USA, the W-4 form determines how much your employer will withhold from your wages. If you leave everything at the default settings, your salary is your only taxable income, and you will only receive the standard deductions. Your employer will calculate your tax withholding based on this information. Employers follow the withholding rates specified in Circular E, issued by the IRS. You can request that additional money be withheld, or you may opt for reduced withholding by claiming extra allowances on your W-4 (for example, beyond just yourself, your spouse, and dependents) if you believe this will result in withholding that more accurately aligns with the tax you owe.
user: Can I choose not to have tax withheld?
assistant: No,the IRS collects taxes from each paycheck throughout the year through a process known as Withholding Tax. The amount withheld by the IRS is determined by the information provided on your W-4 Form, which you submit to your employer when you start a new job. While the IRS no longer requires employers to submit all W-4 forms, they can request a W-4 from any employee at any time.
